protocol: PROTOCOL.md section 7, frozen Arm A prompt, verbatim
operator_note: Single operator who also wrote the answer key. Contamination is unavoidable and applies to both arms equally; the kill criterion rests on the DIFFERENCE. Arm A was generated from the announcement text only, without reopening the key file.
blind_input: vendor announcement only (Scaleway pricing update, 11041 chars). Never shown the thread.

objections.label: STARDUST1-S quadruples overnight
objections.explanation: The cheapest compute tier jumps from €0.00015 to €0.0006 per hour — a 4x increase buried in a table of ~2% adjustments. Entry-level and hobby users chose this tier precisely because it was negligible cost.

objections.label: DNS zone price up 7x
objections.explanation: DNS for external domains goes from €0.001 to €0.007 per hour. Small absolute numbers, but a 7x multiple with no technical justification given, on a service with near-zero marginal cost.

objections.label: Serverless memory bills double unpredictably
objections.explanation: Serverless Jobs, Containers and Functions memory roughly double per GB-second. Bursty workloads that chose serverless for cost control now face unpredictable bills with no cap mentioned.

objections.label: Dedibox customers hit hardest in absolute terms
objections.explanation: Bare-metal Dedibox plans rise 15-17% (e.g. Core-10-S €199.99 to €229.99 monthly). These are the most committed customers with the highest switching costs, and they absorb the largest absolute increases.

objections.label: Partnership language over a unilateral change
objections.explanation: The post frames the hike as something partners do together, but customers get no vote, no opt-out, and no negotiation. The framing invites the exact cynicism it tries to pre-empt.

objections.label: One month notice for budget cycles
objections.explanation: Announced April 27, effective June 1. Teams on quarterly or annual budget cycles cannot replan infrastructure spend in five weeks, so the increase lands as an unbudgeted overrun.

objections.label: No exit assistance; migration costs make it stickier
objections.explanation: Nothing in the announcement addresses portability, migration tooling, or egress terms. A price rise without an exit path reads as confidence that customers cannot easily leave.

objections.label: Key Manager up 50 percent, a tax on good practice
objections.explanation: Version storage goes from €0.04 to €0.06 per key per month. Customers doing the right thing (versioned secrets) pay the steepest proportional increase outside the headline outliers.

objections.label: GPU surcharge lands on AI startups mid-runway
objections.explanation: H100 instances rise ~10% on already-premium hourly rates. Early-stage AI companies with fixed compute budgets and no leverage face an immediate runway hit.

objections.label: No grandfathering for existing customers
objections.explanation: Three years of flat prices are cited as generosity, but existing customers get no loyalty recognition — no phased rollout, no legacy tier, no discount. Loyalty flows one way.
